args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions following the deploy of v2.3.1. Confirmed unhealthy status across us-east, us-west, and eu-west with an error rate of ~18%.

Remediation: Rolled the service back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and the service reports healthy with an error rate of ~0.2%.

Follow-up needed: root cause analysis for the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deploy attempt.

trace.final:
Done — one incident exists, no duplicates.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on v2.3.1 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west, unhealthy with an ~18% error rate. The deployment history showed v2.3.0 as the last healthy production release (the v2.3.1-staging entry was never healthy in production, and v2.3.1 was the unhealthy current release).

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0**.
- First attempt failed partially — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1 (service in a "mixed" state, still unhealthy).
- Retried; the second attempt completed all three regions.
- Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, **healthy**, error rate down from 18% → **0.2%**.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, which paged the on-call engineer. The first create request timed out, so I retried using the same idempotency key; the incident list confirms exactly one incident exists.

**Notes for follow-up:**
- No change-manager approval was required, since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.
- The v2.3.1 regression needs root cause analysis before anyone redeploys it. Consider also reviewing why the orchestrator error interrupted the first rollback mid-rollout, since that left production in a split-version state for a period.
